must_remember: Centripetal force always acts orthogonally to the instantaneous velocity vector and points radially inward.
Centripetal force does zero work on a particle in uniform circular motion because force and displacement are perpendicular.
In uniform circular motion, tangential acceleration is zero, whereas in non-uniform circular motion, both radial and tangential accelerations coexist.
Centrifugal force is a pseudo force of magnitude $m \omega^2 r$ introduced in non-inertial rotating frames.
The minimum speed at the highest point of a vertical loop for a string or track to remain taut is $v_{min} = \sqrt{r g}$.

glossary.meaning: A net inward force directed toward the center of curvature that changes the direction of velocity in circular motion, given by $F_c = \frac{m v^2}{r}$.
An outward fictitious force of magnitude $m \omega^2 r$ experienced in a non-inertial rotating reference frame.
The angle at which a road surface is tilted relative to the horizontal to provide necessary centripetal force without relying solely on friction.
The component of acceleration parallel to the velocity vector, responsible for changing the magnitude of speed in non-uniform circular motion.
